heroText: Augusta is home to Augusta National Golf Club and the Augusta Riverwalk. Its story starts in 1735, when James Oglethorpe sent troops up the river, and Georgia ratified the U.S. Constitution here on January 2, 1788. The Augusta Museum of History, the Sacred Heart Cultural Center and Phinizy Swamp Nature Park complete a visit.

history.text: Establishment In 1735, two years after James Oglethorpe founded Savannah, he sent a detachment of troops to explore the upper Savannah River.
Oglethorpe visited Augusta in September 1739 on his return to Savannah from a perilous visit to Coweta Town, near present-day Phenix City, Alabama.

history.label: 18th century
history.text: The devastating Augusta fire of 1916 damaged 35 blocks of the city's downtown and wiped out many buildings of historical significance, some dating back to the 18th century.
A historical marker in Augusta reads:Augusta served as the capital of Georgia from 1785 until 1795 when the seat of government was moved to the new capital, Louisville.
In Augusta on January 2, 1788, Georgia became the fourth state to ratify the United States Constitution.
In 1789 the General Assembly, meeting here, adopted a new state constitution creating today's bicameral (two-house) state legislature consisting of the Senate and House of Representatives.

history.label: 20th century
history.text: In the mid-20th century, it was a site of civil-rights demonstrations.
In 1970, Charles Oatman, a mentally disabled teenager, was killed by his cellmates in an Augusta jail.
